content_voiceover: This slide compares two important first-line trials in indolent lymphoma. On the left, the German StiL NHL 1-2003 trial randomized five hundred forty-nine patients with follicular, Waldenstrom's, marginal zone, mantle cell, or small lymphocytic lymphoma to bendamustine plus rituximab versus R-CHOP. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, and bendamustine-rituximab showed a strikingly longer median PFS of about sixty-nine and a half months compared to just over thirty-one months with R-CHOP, a hazard ratio of zero point five eight. This established B-R as a preferred first-line regimen with a more favorable toxicity profile. On the right, the GALLIUM trial tested obinutuzumab-based chemoimmunotherapy against rituximab-based chemoimmunotherapy, both followed by maintenance, in over twelve hundred treatment-naive patients with indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma including follicular lymphoma. Investigator-assessed three-year progression-free survival favored the obinutuzumab arm, eighty percent versus seventy-three percent, with a hazard ratio of zero point six six. Together these trials support both bendamustine-rituximab as a backbone regimen and obinutuzumab as a potentially superior anti-CD20 partner for chemoimmunotherapy.
keypoints: StiL trial: bendamustine-rituximab beat R-CHOP in PFS
B-R median PFS about seventy months versus thirty-one months for R-CHOP
GALLIUM: obinutuzumab plus chemo versus rituximab plus chemo
Obinutuzumab arm had better three-year PFS, eighty versus seventy-three percent
keypoint_voiceover: The StiL trial showed bendamustine-rituximab significantly outperforms R-CHOP in progression-free survival for indolent lymphomas, making B-R a preferred first-line backbone. The GALLIUM trial showed obinutuzumab-based chemoimmunotherapy edges out rituximab-based therapy, with three-year PFS of eighty percent versus seventy-three percent.
